items.note: Lab study (N=20) comparing the IdeaSynth research-ideation system with a strong LLM baseline (one AI configuration versus another); outcomes are number of alternative ideas explored and detail of ideas, plus a separate deployment study (N=7); below the 50-person threshold.

Between-subjects experiment (N=79) varying the automation level (low, moderate, high) of a generative AI design tool; outcomes include design time, creative experience, and creative quality (aesthetics, usability) of designs; no no-AI arm, assignment method not stated.

Platform paper (Epitome) that validates itself by replicating three experiments; per search notes one is a Doshi and Hauser (2024) story-writing replication with random assignment to zero, one, or five AI ideas and expert-rated creativity and diversity; the abstract does not name the experiments or sample sizes, so the full text must confirm the story-task design and N.

Within-subjects study (N=20) comparing a multi-agent ideation system (MultiColleagues) with a single-agent baseline; quality and novelty are self-rated by participants, and 'more elaboration during ideation' may be a measured outcome; small sample, same work as arXiv 2510.23904.

Classroom mixed-methods study: 50 undergraduates divided into AI-supported and non-AI teams for the Alternative Uses Task, scored on fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration; assignment method not stated and the analysis unit may be teams.

Evaluative study comparing design inspiration boards made with image-generative AI and with traditional methods on diversity, quantity, fidelity, and ambiguity (AI boards less diverse); abstract does not say who made the boards or whether participants were assigned, so it may instead be an AI-versus-human output comparison.

Reanalysis of the DesignAID experiment data (Cai et al. 2023; 2x2 factorial, Direct versus Diverse LLM idea modes, 111 of 115 users) with a new semantic-area metric; participants who saw more diverse AI ideas selected more diverse but less innovative-rated ideas; shares its sample with the original DesignAID paper. Abstract from the ICCC PDF.

Creative ideation workshop with design-student teams on whether GenAI helps overcome creative fixation, examining team dynamics and creative results; the abstract states no comparison condition or sample size and proposes a conceptual model, so it may be a descriptive case study without a no-AI arm.

Controlled study with 25 design students comparing GPT-4 feedback with feedback from six human educators during brainstorming (AI versus human aid); reported findings are motivation and iterative idea refinement, and it is unclear whether idea creativity was scored; below the 50-person threshold.

AOM poster: lab experiment with 58 participants randomly assigned to a creative product design task with or without ChatGPT; outcomes are psychological ownership and idea championing, and the abstract reports no creativity score of the ideas (the full text could still contain one).
